claims.statement: The in-app notification center's data layer is `api/notification.ts`, which wraps exactly two GET endpoints — `/v1/notification/list` for the first page and `/v1/notification/view-more` with `notification_id` required — and thereafter passes the server's `next_url` through verbatim (carrying the `older_than` cursor for group expansion); no Java change was required because the native API bridge forwards arbitrary paths without an endpoint whitelist.

Notification response types are deliberately permissive — every field except `id` and `created_datetime` is optional — and rendering depends on `content.text` with `type` treated as a hint only, so a new server-side notification `type` value cannot break parsing.

Unread is derived locally, not from the server's `is_read`: `countUnreadNotifications` counts entries whose `created_datetime` parses to a millisecond value strictly later than the device-level `notifications_last_read_time` timestamp, counts every parsable entry when the key is absent, and excludes an unparsable entry while warning instead of degrading silently.

The read timestamp advances only after a successful notification-list fetch: the notifications page watches `list.isSuccess` and calls `notifyListLoaded(true)`, which writes the current timestamp and zeroes the badge, while a failed fetch never advances it and a failed write warns and leaves the old value so unread is not lost.

Posting a probe system notification must not advance the local read memory: the trigger chain never calls `markNotificationsRead`, and the contract gate asserts that absence so that the badge and the probe's own comparison baseline cannot be erased by its own send.

`refreshUnreadBadge()` returns a boolean because on failure it keeps the previous `unreadCount`; callers that treat the count as fresh input (notably the delivery probe) must check that return value, and the trigger treats a failed refresh as no unread instead of using the stale count.

The unread badge value is read at three points — the radial FAB's `navBadge` for the `updates` ring item, the Me entry row's dot, and the Updates page segment — and it is prefetched once at cold start in `App.vue` and re-refreshed by `Me.vue` in `onActivated`, because Me lives inside the KeepAlive include where `onMounted` fires only once per session.

Group-header expansion is modelled as a flat row list where `view_more != null` marks a header and expanding only flips a boolean on an existing row (stable `h-{id}` / `n-{id}` keys, one-way, no collapse), so the native list's row count never changes; the child list renders inside the header row's own `list-item` root because inserting a `list-item` mid-list is silently dropped by the Lynx patch layer.

`notificationPlainText` strips all HTML tags while keeping inner text, decodes a fixed entity subset in a single pass (so `&lt;` decodes one level, matching DOM semantics), trims, and maps null/undefined to an empty string; the result is never handed to an HTML rendering channel.

`target_url` routing is a pure string-based resolver plus a thin jump layer: `pixiv://users|illusts|novels/{numeric-id}` maps to `/user/{id}` / `/illust/{id}` / the novel entry point, `http(s)` goes to the system browser, and every other case — unknown scheme, unknown host segment, empty or non-numeric id, missing value — is silently ignored rather than thrown; parsing is string-based because the Lynx URL polyfill has no working `hostname`.

Notification thumbnails are routed through `proxyImageUrl`, which rewrites `i.pximg.net` paths to the local `/pixiv-img/` path, passes other trusted `*.pximg.net` hosts (the public `s.pximg.net` icons) through unchanged, and returns an empty string for untrusted hosts; a row's image area is hidden after a load failure, keyed per row to avoid a retry storm, and `left_image` is preferred over `left_icon`.

`pages/Updates.vue` is not the notification center: its third segment reads the store's shared infinite-query cache instead of calling the endpoint again (so the badge and the preview come from one response), and it derives unread with the same rule into a page-local `unreadCount` ref that is a different variable from `notificationStore.unreadCount` — the degradation path and the probe must use the store's value.

The delivery probe is framed as a measurement rather than a feature: acceptance is one decidable data point about whether the user wants the receipt, it measures only `clicked ÷ sent` against how often the user opens the app unprompted, it sets no statistical threshold because a single user's sample ceiling is their open frequency (on the order of 14 sent samples a week), and its conclusions are therefore qualitative — "nobody clicked" can argue against server push while "somebody clicked" cannot be generalised.

The probe triggers on "entered foreground plus quiet period", not on `WorkManager` scheduling (deliberate deviation from ADR-0188's Phase 2 wording): the host emits `pictelioAppForeground` in `onResume` and `pictelioAppBackground` in `onPause` via the same `sendGlobalEvent` mechanism as the insets and dark-mode events, and JS approximates "the user is not actively looking" from those lifecycle events because the Lynx side has no window-focus event.

Cold-start backfill is mandatory: because Android's `onResume` precedes JS mount the first foreground event is always lost, so on subscribe the lifecycle module treats "subscribed" as currently foreground, records the instant, and schedules a round — both the event path and the backfill path schedule, and the contract gate pins each of them separately so one cannot be dropped silently.

Every foreground/background transition increments a generation counter, and a scheduled round captures that generation and re-checks it after each `await` (permission query, unread refresh) before posting, so a round still in flight when the user leaves is abandoned; a plain "is the app foreground now" test would let a stale round double-post after backgrounding and returning.

The send decision is a pure function, `decideProbe`, whose ordering is the semantics — a 90-second quiet period first, then `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` permission, then a non-zero unread count — and every round logs its decision reason whether or not it sends, because otherwise a report cannot distinguish "nobody clicked" from "nothing was ever sent".

One poll produces exactly one aggregated notification, counted as one sent sample regardless of how many updates the batch contains; the body states only the count and never the notification text, the wording and channel names are assembled in the host from a locale string JS passes in, and a fixed notification id makes consecutive rounds overwrite instead of stack.

The notification channel must actually be registered, not merely constructed: a "channel" object that is never passed to `createNotificationChannel` makes Android 8+ drop the notification silently, which the probe would then read as nobody clicking — the contract gate targets the call specifically and a fixture proves the weaker assertion cannot catch it.

The native notification bridge only queries permission and never requests `POST_NOTIFICATIONS`: `areNotificationsEnabled` reads the real `NotificationManager` state, a query failure resolves as not granted so the caller degrades to the already-shipped unread badge, and the callback contract forbids passing null — meaning a fresh install is structurally data-free unless permission is granted out of band.

Probe counts are one JSON value `{ sent, clicked, startedAt }` under the key `delivery_probe_v1` in the shared `CapacitorStorage` preferences file (IndexedDB in dev) rather than three keys, so a reset can clear the counters and keep `startedAt` in one atomic write; `startedAt` is stamped on the first send and preserved by `resetRound()`, keeping successive rounds on one timeline.

Missing, malformed, or partially malformed counter values fall back per field as "no round has run yet" with an explicit warning, and the native preference bridge's JSON-quoted strings must be run through `unquoteNativeString` before `JSON.parse`; a silent fallback or a missed unquote would turn real device counts into a zero denominator that reads as "nobody clicked".

The counter key has a single-writer invariant: only JS writes `delivery_probe_v1`, and the contract gate scans both the notification module and the host Activity to assert the native side never touches it, because two writers would split the count into two partial truths.

The probe has no product UI to read it: the operator extracts the counter JSON from `shared_prefs/CapacitorStorage.xml` (mindful that `"` is XML-layer escaping while JS receives real quotes) and the permission state from `dumpsys package ... POST_NOTIFICATIONS`, then feeds both into `buildProbeReport`; `resetRound()` currently has no production call site.

The click landing chain runs from the notification's `PendingIntent` (which targets `NotificationTapActivity`, a `NoDisplay` Activity exempt from Android 10+ background-Activity-launch limits because the system started it) through the forwarded target/clickId extras into `LynxActivity`, which persists the pending click id synchronously, broadcasts `pictelioNotificationTarget` at four fixed delays, and lets JS dedupe by click id, record one click and navigate to `/notifications` with push rather than replace.

Click deduplication by `clickId` is required because navigation is idempotent but counting is not: the host generates one click id per delivery so the four rebroadcasts share it, JS accepts only the first arrival within a bounded seen-set, and the tap intent must carry that id through both hops or every click would collapse onto the same key and freeze the counter.

The broadcast count is fixed at four and the earlier "single broadcast / multi-window" criteria were removed: both candidate criteria were falsified on device, so redundant arrivals are absorbed by click-id dedupe instead — the same fix shape as two prior reporting mistakes in this workstream, where the answer was to delete a criterion rather than make it cleverer.

Cold and warm clicks are deliberately not separable in the counter: an earlier `clickedCold` / `clickedWarm` design was withdrawn after four candidate in-process criteria (lifecycle callback type, in-process static flag, persisted foreground marker, process lifetime) were falsified on device because handling the tap is itself the state transition, so only the total `clicked` is kept and the report must not present it as the share of users called back from the tray.

Warm-start taps must override `onNewIntent` and call `setIntent(intent)` before dispatching the target, otherwise `getIntent()` keeps returning the launch intent and the click extras are dropped silently, producing a tap that appears to do nothing.

The probe report encodes its honesty rules rather than leaving them to the reader: the rate is `null` (never 0) when nothing was sent or clicks exceed sends, the `no-data` verdict takes precedence over `not-clicked` and covers both a zero denominator and denied permission, permission has three states with `null` mapped to `unknown` rather than denied, contradictory counts surface as `anomalies`, and four fixed caveats in stable order travel with every report.

The probe's own landing target contaminates its input across rounds: the notification center's successful fetch advances the read memory, so unread drops to zero and a subsequent round decides `no-unread` and never posts — a new round needs both a counter reset and a rewound `notifications_last_read_time`, which the cold-start e2e performs as step 0.

The JS↔Java boundary is pinned by a contract gate that reads the host Java and manifest sources, strips comments, extracts the event names from the JS source, requires both sides to contain each symbol, compares the full expected set of `mod.*` calls against the module's `@LynxMethod` declarations, and asserts the channel-registration call and the `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` declaration — with fixture self-checks so no detector is vacuously true.

The host side of the probe is a thin bridge plus one Activity: `PictelioNotificationModule` is registered as `PictelioNotification` in `LynxRuntimeInitializer`, the manifest declares `POST_NOTIFICATIONS`, and `NotificationTapActivity` is declared non-exported with `excludeFromRecents`, `noHistory` and a `NoDisplay` theme so that only the app's own notification `PendingIntent` can trigger it and inflate the click count.

The pull half of the click landing is unproven on device: the host writes the pending click id into the `CapacitorStorage` preferences file while `pullPendingClick` reads it through `idbGet`, the IndexedDB KV store, and the contract gate pins only the key string and the existence of both calls, not that the two sides agree on a store.

This domain's focused tests are split across three tiers: Vitest unit tests for store, report, landing, target, text and the captured API fixtures; JVM/Robolectric tests that drive the notification module's static seams and assert against the system notification and channel tables; and a manual, non-CI Android e2e cold-start gate that asserts from native log lines and is explicitly an addition to, not a replacement for, the unit and contract gates.
